topic: sub:11|Working with functions|Direct and inverse variation

parts.latex:
It is given that a quantity $y$ varies inversely with the square of $x$.

When $x=4$, $y=10$.

Find the value of $y$ when $x=5$.

solutions.latex:
$y$ varies inversely with the square of $x$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&\propto\dfrac{1}{x^2}\\ y&=\dfrac{k}{x^2}\end{aligned}$$
Substitute $x=4$, $y=10$ to find $k$:
$$\begin{aligned}10&=\dfrac{k}{4^2}\\ k&=160\end{aligned}$$
$$y=\dfrac{160}{x^2}$$
Substitute $x=5$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=\dfrac{160}{5^2}\\ &=6.4\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: Which of the following represents an inverse variation relationship?

solutions.latex:
Inverse variation is of the form $y=\dfrac{k}{x}$, where $k$ is the constant of variation.

Only $y=\dfrac{4}{x}$ has this form (with $k=4$); the others are direct variation or exponential.

parts.latex:
Trish is planning a function. The cost per person to attend the function varies inversely with the number of people attending.

The cost per person is \$70 when 50 people attend.

What is the cost per person if 125 people attend the function?

solutions.latex:
Let $x$ be the number of people and $y$ the cost per person in dollars.

Inverse variation has the form
$$y=\dfrac{k}{x}$$
When $x=50$, $y=70$, hence
$$\begin{aligned} k&=xy\\ &=50\times70\\ &=3500 \end{aligned}$$
When $x=125$:
$$y=\dfrac{3500}{125}=28$$
$\therefore$ The cost is \$28 per person if 125 people attend.

1052.stem:
The wavelength, $\lambda$ metres, of a musical tone is inversely proportional to its frequency, $f$ vibrations per second.

The frequency of middle C is approximately 260 vibrations per second and its wavelength is approximately 1.32 m.

parts.latex: Write an equation to represent this, in the form $\lambda=g(f)$.
Hence, find the frequency, in vibrations per second, of a sound wave with wavelength 0.8 m.

solutions.latex:
Since $\lambda$ is inversely proportional to $f$:
$$\lambda=\dfrac{k}{f}$$
Substituting $f=260$, $\lambda=1.32$:
$$\begin{aligned}1.32&=\dfrac{k}{260}\\k&=260\times1.32=343.2\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\lambda=\dfrac{343.2}{f}$$

From part (a), with $\lambda=0.8$:
$$\begin{aligned}f&=\dfrac{343.2}{\lambda}\\&=\dfrac{343.2}{0.8}\\&=429\text{ vibrations per second}\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: It is given that $y$ is inversely proportional to $x$.
When $x=9$, $y=3$. Determine the equation relating $x$ in terms of $y$.
If the value of $x$ is increased from 2 to 18, determine the change in the value of $y$.
Hence graph the relationship between $x$ and $y$ using the values you have found previously.

solutions.latex:
For inverse proportion, $y=\dfrac{k}{x}$.

Substituting $x=9$, $y=3$:
$$\begin{aligned}3&=\dfrac{k}{9}\\ k&=27\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ y=\dfrac{27}{x}$$
